name: Binaural Study Hall
description: Classical music for studying, reading and writing, built for headphones: a prelude over a soft alpha beat, a string quartet seated around you, a sarabande over a pad that spreads from the centre to all around you, a larghetto whose strings breathe apart in cents, a slowly rotating chorale, an etude whose brightness wanders between the ears, a two-part invention with one voice in each ear, a nocturne in a wide, quiet reading room, a baroque allegretto over a beta beat and a harp minuet over a delta drone to close the books. Slow tempos, gentle levels and nothing sudden; each sketch explains its trick in the comments. Headphones on, volume low.
author: Claude, for Tartlet

sketches.name: Alpha Prelude
sketches.description: A prelude of broken chords in C, the same in both ears, over a cello and a quiet 10 Hz binaural drone in the alpha range. The beat forms only between the ears, so on speakers you hear a plain drone. The player asks before playing, as with any steady pulse.
sketches.source:
setcpm(60/4)

// A prelude of broken chords, the same in both ears: C, Am, Dm7, G7
prelude: note("<[c3 e3 g3 c4 e4 g3 c4 e4] [a2 e3 a3 c4 e4 a3 c4 e4] [d3 f3 a3 c4 f4 a3 c4 f4] [g2 d3 g3 b3 f4 g3 b3 f4]>")
  .s("triangle").timbre("soft").attack(.005).decay(1.2).sustain(.08).release(1.4)
  .lpf(2200).room(.5).size(.8).gain(.26)

// A cello holds each root, centred
cello: note("<c2 a1 d2 g1>").s("sawtooth").vib(4.5).vibdepth(.08).lpf(600)
  .attack(.6).sustain(.7).release(1.2).room(.5).gain(.16)

// A 10 Hz binaural beat in the alpha range: each ear is detuned by 5 Hz. Keep it quiet
drone: note("[c3,g3]").slow(4).s("sine").binaural(10)
  .attack(3).sustain(1).release(4).gain(.1)

sketches.name: Seated Quartet
sketches.description: An andante in F for string quartet, seated in a semicircle in front of you as on a concert stage: first violin far left, second violin left of centre, viola right of centre and cello on the right.
sketches.source:
setcpm(72/4)

// One bowed string, named once; the brightness has a default
const bowed = (x, bright = 2400) => x.s("sawtooth").vib(5).vibdepth(.1)
  .attack(.08).sustain(.7).release(.4).lpf(bright)

// The players sit in a semicircle in front of you: 0 is straight ahead, negative is left
// F, Dm, Bb, C7
violin1: note("<[a4@3 g4 f4@2 a4@2] [d5@4 c5@2 a4@2] [bb4@3 a4 g4@2 f4 d4] [e4@2 g4@2 c5@4]>")
  .bowed(3000).azimuth(-50).distance(2.5).room(.4).gain(.2)
violin2: note("<[c4 f4] [f4 a4] [d4 f4] [e4 g4]>")
  .bowed().azimuth(-18).distance(2.5).room(.4).gain(.15)
viola: note("<a3 a3 bb3 bb3>")
  .bowed(1800).azimuth(18).distance(2.5).room(.4).gain(.14)
cello: note("<[f2 c3] [d2 a2] [bb1 f2] [c2 g2]>")
  .bowed(900).azimuth(50).distance(2.5).room(.4).gain(.22)

sketches.name: Sarabande in Phase
sketches.description: A harpsichord sarabande in D minor, with its weight on the second beat, sits in the centre of your head while a string pad underneath steps from in phase to 90 and 180 degrees, two bars at a time, spreading from a point into a haze. On speakers the 180-degree bars of the pad nearly vanish.

sketches.name: Larghetto in Cents
sketches.description: A slow piano larghetto in G over strings whose ears drift apart in cents and back again: 3 cents beats slowly, 8 shimmers and 15 widens like a larger section. The piano and cello stay true in the centre.

sketches.name: Lento for Flute and Organ
sketches.description: A slow flute melody in E-flat sings in the centre while the organ chords underneath turn their interaural phase, from once every five seconds to just under once a second, so the harmony drifts gently around inside your head. All rates stay well below 3 Hz.

sketches.name: Wandering Etude
sketches.description: A flowing piano etude in E minor where nothing is panned, yet the brightness drifts from ear to ear: a low-pass on each ear alone sweeps in opposite directions every eight bars. The inner voices are thinner on the right, where a high-pass cuts their body.

sketches.name: Invention for Two Ears
sketches.description: A two-part invention in C with one voice in each ear: the upper line leans right and the lower line left through a level difference, and on every fourth bar they trade places. Easy to follow, and a gentle way to hear counterpoint as two separate lines.
sketches.source:
setcpm(84/4)

// ild makes the right ear louder; earswap flips the ears on the steps marked 1
// The upper voice leans right, the lower left; every fourth bar they swap
upper: note("<[c5 d5 e5 f5 d5 e5 c5 g5] [c6@2 b5 c6 d6@2 g5@2] [a5 g5 f5 e5 d5 f5 e5 d5] [c5@4 ~@4]>")
  .s("triangle").timbre("bright").ild(6).earswap("<0 0 0 1>")
  .attack(.003).decay(.3).sustain(.2).release(.2).room(.4).gain(.22)
lower: note("<[c3@2 e3@2 g3@2 e3@2] [g2@2 b2@2 g3@2 b2@2] [f2@2 a2@2 g2@2 b2@2] [c3@4 g2 a2 b2 c3]>")
  .s("square").pw(.25).lpf(1800).ild(6).earswap("<1 1 1 0>")
  .attack(.003).decay(.3).sustain(.3).release(.2).room(.4).gain(.14)

sketches.name: Reading Room Nocturne
sketches.description: Headphones on: a nocturne in A in a quiet reading room. The air of the room is wide and diffuse, a fire crackles to your left, a clock ticks on the right and rain falls outside, behind the glass.
sketches.source:
setcpm(58/4)

// Left hand: broken chords through A, F#m, D and E
left: note("<[a2 e3 c#4 e3 a3 e3 c#4 e3] [f#2 c#3 a3 c#3 f#3 c#3 a3 c#3] [d2 a2 f#3 a2 d3 a2 f#3 a2] [e2 b2 g#3 b2 e3 b2 g#3 b2]>")
  .s("triangle").timbre("soft").attack(.005).decay(.9).sustain(.1).release(1.2)
  .lpf(1800).room(.5).gain(.26)

// Right hand: the song, in the centre of your head
right: note("<[e5@3 d5 c#5@2 e5@2] [c#5@4 b4@2 a4@2] [a4@3 b4 d5@2 f#5@2] [e5@6 ~@2]>")
  .s("sine").fm(.8).fmh(2).attack(.01).decay(1.4).sustain(.2).release(1.5)
  .room(.6).gain(.3)

// The air of the room: unrelated noise in each ear, wide and enveloping
air: s("pink").slow(8).icorr(.15).hpf(600).lpf(3000).gain(.025)

// A fire on your left, a clock on your right, rain beyond the window
fire: s("fire").slow(4).intensity(.25).density(5).azimuth(-60).distance(3).gain(.14)
clock: s("tick ~ tick ~").azimuth(70).distance(4).gain(.05)
rain: s("rain").slow(4).intensity(.35).occlude(.6).gain(.16)

sketches.name: Beta Allegretto
sketches.description: A baroque allegretto in G for violin, harpsichord continuo and cello, over a very quiet 14 Hz binaural drone in the beta range. The continuo sends its lows to one ear and its highs to the other; together, and in mono, it sounds whole. The player asks before playing, as with any steady pulse.
sketches.source:
setcpm(96/4)

// The violin runs in eighths through G, C, D and G, the same in both ears
violin: n("0 2 4 2 5 4 2 4").add("<0 3 4 0>").scale("G:major").transpose(12)
  .s("sawtooth").vib(5).vibdepth(.08).lpf(3000)
  .attack(.02).decay(.2).sustain(.5).release(.1).room(.4).gain(.18)

// earsplit("bands") puts the continuo's lows in one ear and its highs in the other
continuo: note("<[g3,b3,d4] [c4,e4,g4] [d4,f#4,a4] [g3,b3,d4]>").struct("x ~ x ~")
  .s("square").pw(.15).earsplit("bands").splitfreq(800)
  .decay(.25).sustain(0).lpf(3200).room(.3).gain(.12)

// The cello on root and fifth, centred
cello: note("<[g2 d2] [c3 g2] [d3 a2] [g2 d2]>").s("sawtooth").lpf(700)
  .attack(.04).sustain(.6).release(.3).room(.4).gain(.22)

// A 14 Hz binaural beat in the beta range: each ear is detuned by 7 Hz. Keep it very quiet
drone: note("[g2,d3]").slow(4).s("sine").binaural(14)
  .attack(3).sustain(1).release(4).gain(.08)

sketches.name: Closing the Books
sketches.description: The end of the session: a slow harp minuet in B-flat floating a little above your head, over a 2 Hz binaural drone in the delta range, below the rates that trigger a pulse warning, with crickets far away.
